pnl_definition: Net trading revenue of DRW's trading businesses: DRW Holdings LLC / DRW Trading Group and its trading affiliates globally, including Cumberland DRW. It means trading gains net of direct trading costs (exchange, clearing and brokerage fees, execution costs, and financing of trading positions), before compensation and other operating expenses. Calendar year, USD millions. Excluded: DRW Venture Capital, commercial real estate (Convexity) and Don Wilson's personal investments. Interest on the holding company's term loan is not deducted, for comparability with peers' reported net trading revenue (for example Virtu's ANTI, which excludes corporate-debt interest). The ratings agencies note that the loan proceeds partly fund trading capital. Rough size of that interest, not reported: about $20-25m in 2021, $25-40m in 2022, $70-80m in 2023, $80-90m in 2024 and $90-100m in 2025, on $500m rising to $900m and then $1.15bn. The only firm-wide figure is Bloomberg's FY2020 holding-level 'revenue' of about $1.5bn. It is not known whether that figure is gross or net of trading costs, so it was converted with a blended haircut: about 8-9% for probable trading costs (the gross and net readings weighted roughly 50/50) plus about 6% for VC and real estate (5-10% of net revenue per S&P), giving about $1.27bn. net_income_usd_m has three uses, all proxies. 2019 and 2020 are holding-level profit proxies derived from reported or implied EBITDA, and they include VC and real estate. 2026 Q1 records the reported 'adjusted loss of $176m', whose definition is unknown.
headcount_definition: Total employees of DRW's trading group, all functions and offices, excluding contractors where possible. Values are approximate year-end (31 Dec) point estimates. The exception is 2026, which is an approximate Q1 2026 average to match the Q1-only PnL. Each year is built bottom-up from three inputs: US 401(k) active participants at plan year-end from DOL Form 5500 (DRW Holdings LLC), which is a US-only floor; DRW UK Partners LLP average staff from Companies House, adjusted toward year-end; and estimates for Canada, Singapore and Hong Kong, the Netherlands, Israel and other offices. The bottom-up totals are anchored to dated firm-wide figures: 725 (Reuters, Dec 2016), about 900 (eFC, Oct 2018), over 1,000 (Moody's, Nov 2019), about 1,700 (The TRADE, Jul 2023) and about 2,100 (FT, Nov 2024). Annual average headcount runs about 2-11% below year-end in growth years: about 6% in 2021, 9-10% in 2022 and 9-11% in 2023. Each row's notes give the approximate average. PnL per head computed on year-end heads therefore understates per-average-head productivity by up to about 11% in fast-growth years compared with peers that report average FTE.
fx_note: The PnL anchors are already in USD: DRW Investments, LLC's US GAAP accounts, Bloomberg's FY2020 figures, the FT and eFC, and the SEC complaint. GBP figures from DRW UK Partners LLP (staff costs, performance fees, turnover) are used only as scaling and direction indicators, converted at the orchestrator's annual-average GBPUSD rates: 2020 1.284, 2021 1.376, 2022 1.237, 2023 1.244, 2024 1.278, 2025 about 1.32. The 2015-2024 rates match known annual averages. The 2025 rate was kept as given, because no web check was possible (search budget exhausted); an error of +/-0.02 would move the 2025 UK cost per head by about 1.5% and the row by less than that. UK all-in staff cost per head: 2020 £422k ($542k), 2021 £399k ($549k), 2022 £570k ($705k), 2023 £312k ($388k, on £76.03m and 244 average staff as shown in the FY2024 comparative), 2024 £371k ($474k), 2025 £400k ($528k). DRW Singapore Pte Ltd figures are in SGD (functional currency confirmed by the source auditor) and are used only for year-on-year direction. They are not converted into any row value. No EUR figures were used.
methodology:
There is one firm-wide PnL anchor. Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021, people familiar, during a loan process) reported FY2020 revenue of about $1.5bn (+50%) and EBITDA of about $750m (+67%). FY2019 is implied from those growth rates. Both years were converted to the project definition with a blended haircut. One reading is that Bloomberg's 'revenue' is gross: DRW's audited DRWI accounts present 'Total revenue' before trading expenses of 12.7-22.4% of revenue. The other is that it is net: S&P speaks of 'net revenue'. The two readings were weighted roughly 50/50, and 5-10% for VC and real estate (S&P) was removed. Result: 2020 about $1.27bn, 2019 about $0.83bn.

2015-2018: the hard anchor is the audited net trading revenue of DRW Investments, LLC (DRWI), DRW's main US prop-trading entity, which filed whole-entity accounts at Companies House to FY2018. It was scaled to the group by an assumed DRWI share of group PnL. The share path runs about 55% in 2015-16, 51% in 2017 and 38.5% in 2018. In 2018 it is cross-checked against the Bloomberg-implied 2019 group figure, a 34-38% share.

2021-2025: no figures exist. Firm compensation = 0.7 (range 0.55-0.9) x the UK LLP's audited all-in staff cost per head x average firm headcount. That comp is divided by a comp ratio anchored at the ~32% the 2020 calibration implies, moving up to 35-37% only where DRW-specific evidence supports it: S&P's 'good, but not as strong' as peers in 2024, and UK pay outrunning UK performance fees in 2025. Judgment trims are applied only for identified UK-specific effects, such as the 2022 European energy-desk outperformance, and are applied symmetrically, so 2023 is untrimmed. Direction is cross-checked against UK LLP performance fees from affiliates and members, UK turnover and operating profit, DRW Singapore results (taking account of transfer-pricing and booking changes), rating-agency text and peer regimes (Optiver, IMC and Virtu primary figures).

Consequence: for 2021-2025, PnL per head is essentially the UK pay per head times 0.7 divided by the comp ratio. It is model-derived, and PnL and headcount errors are positively correlated by construction.

2026: Q1 only, from the FT's 'adjusted loss of $176m' as relayed by eFC. Scope and definition are unresolved, so three scenarios are weighted: firm-level after costs about 55%, trading-level about 20%, desk-only about 25%. The rest-of-firm run-rate in the desk-only scenario is valued at the strong Q1 2026 industry regime.

Headcount: bottom-up from DOL Form 5500 US 401(k) counts and UK LLP accounts, plus office estimates, anchored to dated press and rating-agency counts.

The reconciler ran no new web searches (shared budget exhausted). It directly fetched or OCR'd: the UK LLP FY2024 accounts (2023 comparative staff costs and headcount), the UK LLP 2022 related-party note (performance fees from members) and Virtu's Q1 2026 8-K. It also probed Troubled Company Reporter issues after 28 Jul 2026; none are online.

entities.name: DRW (firm-wide)
entities.description: DRW Holdings LLC / DRW Trading Group and its trading affiliates globally: DRW Investments LLC, DRW Canada/Vigilant, DRW Singapore and DRW Europe B.V., the UK entities, Houston energy, the former Chopper and RGM teams, and Cumberland DRW (crypto). Excludes DRW Venture Capital, commercial real estate (Convexity) and Don Wilson's personal investments.

rows.notes: PnL is derived from a hard floor. DRW Investments, LLC (DRWI; main US prop-trading entity including its UK branch; audited US GAAP accounts at Companies House) had FY2015 total revenue of $470.4m less trading expenses (commissions/execution and interest) of $59.6m, giving $410.8m net trading revenue, up 34% from $306.7m in FY2014. Entity net income was $272.4m after $72.2m compensation. Other units sat outside or alongside DRWI: Chopper Trading (acquired Jan 2015; booking entity unknown), DRW Canada/Vigilant, DRW Europe, the new Singapore office and a small Cumberland. The group figure assumes DRWI was 41-76% of group PnL (mid 55%). That share is higher than the 2018 share (~38.5%) because the group was less diversified in 2015. No firm-wide revenue figure exists for 2015. Headcount: US 401(k) active participants at 31 Dec 2015 were 497 (welfare plan 517) and UK LLP average staff was 32. Bloomberg (Jan 2015) said 'more than 500' before Chopper, which itself had 'more than 200'. Net retention of Chopper staff was about 100: Chopper's 401(k) fell from 190 to 9 active while DRW's rose from 394 to 497. Bloomberg (Mar 2016) said '700-person'. Bottom-up: US ~500 + UK ~32 + Canada ~130 (estimated) + Singapore ~15 + other ~25, about 700. Average heads in 2015 about 660.

PnL is derived. DRWI FY2016 net trading revenue was $378.8m ($454.8m revenue less $76.0m trading expenses), down 8%; entity net income was $245.6m. The group figure is DRWI divided by an assumed share of 41-76% (mid 55%), the same structure as 2015. RGM Advisors was not yet acquired (80 active in its own 401(k) at end-2016) and Cumberland was small. Market regime was moderate (Brexit, US election). No firm-wide revenue figure was found. Headcount: Reuters (1 Dec 2016) described 'his privately held 725-employee company, DRW Holdings LLC', a specific, non-round number. US 401(k) active participants at end-2016 were 500 (welfare plan 525), a US share of about 0.69. Bloomberg (Mar 2016) said '700-person'. UK LLP average staff was 38. Average heads in 2016 about 710.

PnL is derived. DRWI FY2017 net trading revenue was $404.9m ($487.2m revenue less $82.2m trading expenses), up 7%; entity net income was $269.6m. Units added since 2016: Cumberland in the 2017 crypto boom (WSJ, Dec 2017, company-reported: more than $20bn of crypto traded in the year; volume, not revenue), RGM Advisors (Austin, about 70 staff), the Houston energy team (Nov 2017) and DRW Singapore (company-only total net revenue S$40.3m, profit before tax S$1.6m). The DRWI share is assumed at 37-70% (mid ~51%), on a path from 55% in 2016 to 38.5% in 2018. 2017 was a low-volatility year for markets broadly; peers Optiver and IMC were down. The FT's 'single London-based subsidiary [that] made almost $1bn in revenue over 2017 and 2018' is DRWI itself ($487m + $376m = $863m of total revenue before about $82-84m a year of trading costs), not an additional entity. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 580 (welfare plan 603) and UK average staff was 49. 580/0.69 gives about 840, between Reuters' 725 (Dec 2016) and eFC's ~900 (Oct 2018). Average heads in 2017 about 785.

PnL is derived. DRWI FY2018 net trading revenue was $292.1m ($376.2m revenue less $84.1m trading expenses: $65.2m commissions/fees and $18.4m interest), down 28%; entity net income was $131.2m. This was DRWI's last filing (its UK establishment closed Feb 2020). The DRWI share is now assumed at 26.5-58% (mid 38.5%), revised from the draft's 42%. The draft's own cross-check against Bloomberg-implied 2019 group figures gives 34% (net) to 38% (revenue). Peers had a stronger 2018 than 2017 or 2019 (Optiver $1,535m vs $919m/$1,269m; IMC $709m vs $417m/$520m), and part of DRWI's fall may reflect booking moving to other entities, such as DRW Europe B.V. ahead of Brexit (unproven). Other units grew: DRW Singapore total net revenue S$83.7m vs S$40.3m, profit before tax S$15.9m. Cumberland's only figure is the SEC allegation of more than $400m revenue from Mar 2018 to Oct 2024, about $60m+ a year on average, in a case dismissed in Mar 2025. RGM, Houston, Canada and Europe also contributed. Result: $292.1m / 0.385 = about $760m (range about $500m to $1.1bn). Headcount: eFC (8 Oct 2018) said DRW 'employs about 900 people globally'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 614 (welfare plan 633). UK average staff was 58; Singapore about 40. Average heads in 2018 about 870.

PnL is derived from Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021; people familiar; loan-marketing context). 2020 revenue rose 50% to about $1.5bn and EBITDA rose 67% to about $750m, implying 2019 revenue of about $1.0bn (about $0.94-1.07bn given rounding) and EBITDA of about $450m. It is unknown whether 'revenue' is gross or net of trading costs. DRW's audited DRWI accounts present gross 'Total revenue' with trading expenses of 12.7-22.4% below it (22.4% in 2018), while S&P refers to 'net revenue'. The two readings were weighted about 50/50. Gross reading: a 13-18% trading-cost haircut plus 5-10% for VC and real estate gives about $760-830m. Net reading: about $880-950m. Mid $830m, lowered from $860m after the source auditor's challenge. net_income_usd_m is a proxy, not reported: implied EBITDA of about $450m less small term-loan interest (first $300m loan Nov 2019), depreciation and amortisation, and foreign taxes. It is holding-level and includes VC and real estate. DRW Singapore company-only revenue was flat at S$83.7m. Headcount: Moody's (7 Nov 2019) said 'the firm has grown steadily to over 1000 employees operating in ten offices'. That is a floor, so the low is now 1,000. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 688 (welfare plan 676) and UK average staff was 65 (Apr-Dec 2019). Average heads in 2019 about 965.

This is the only firm-wide annual PnL figure found. Bloomberg (18 Jun 2021): 'At futures, options and cryptocurrencies trader DRW Holdings LLC, revenue and Ebitda surged in 2020 by 50% and 67%, respectively, to about $1.5 billion and $750 million, people familiar with the matter said.' It was verified only through matching syndicated snippets; Bloomberg returned 403. S&P (Feb 2021) said 'profitability was up considerably in 2020... While some peers posted even stronger results'. The basis label changed from reported_press to derived, because the row value is a conversion of an undefined holding-level 'revenue'. Gross reading (DRW's audited format; trading costs 11-17% of revenue, at the low end in a high-volume year), with 5-10% removed for VC and real estate: about $1.15-1.29bn. Net reading: about $1.35-1.43bn. The ~50/50 blend gives a mid of $1.27bn. The low of $1.0bn allows gross revenue, a larger VC/crypto-equity share in 2020 and rounding of 'about'; the high of $1.55bn allows net revenue and a small VC share. Corroboration: DRW Singapore company-only revenue more than doubled to S$195m (profit before tax S$84m). Calibration for 2021-2025: 0.7 x UK all-in staff cost per head ($542k) x ~1,065 average heads gives about $405m of comp, about 32% of $1.27bn, consistent with a ~50% EBITDA margin on gross revenue. net_income_usd_m is a proxy, not reported: EBITDA of about $750m less interest on the ~$300m term loan, depreciation and amortisation, and foreign taxes. It is holding-level and includes VC and real estate. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 746 (+8%; welfare plan 718) and UK average staff was 63. Bottom-up: US 746 + UK ~70 + Canada ~170 (estimated) + Singapore ~45 + other ~40, about 1,070. The headcount was raised to about 1,100, low 1,030, because the same method undershot Moody's '>1,000' floor in Nov 2019 by about 30-50. Average heads in 2020 about 1,065.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. Comp-scaling: 0.7 x UK all-in cost per head ($549k; £37.5m / 94) x ~1,165 average heads gives about $448m of firm comp. At the 2020-calibrated ~32% comp ratio that implies about $1.40bn (31% gives $1.45bn; 35% gives $1.28bn). The mid was raised from $1.35bn, which used an un-evidenced 31-35% band. Signals are mixed. Positives: the crypto boom (Cumberland; DRW VC gains are out of scope), UK LLP turnover £66.6m to £80.3m (+21%), UK performance fees from affiliates £67.4m, and UK cost per head flat. Negatives: DRW Singapore company-only revenue fell 42% to S$112.5m (profit before tax S$24.8m vs S$84m). Peers were mixed (Optiver -25%, IMC flat, Virtu -16%). The draft's Moody's quote ('strong performance thus far in 2021', at an Oct 2021 upgrade to Ba2) is not in the cited TCR issue and is unverified; Moody's did rate DRW Ba2 by Dec 2024. The $500m term loan was refinanced in Feb 2021; its interest (about $20-25m) is not deducted. Bars run -36%/+46%: the UK-to-firm pay factor (0.55-0.9), the comp ratio and UK representativeness are all assumptions. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 826 (+11%; welfare plan 800) and UK average staff was 94. Bottom-up: US 826 + UK ~120 + Canada ~190 (estimated) + Singapore ~50 + other ~40, about 1,230. Average heads in 2021 about 1,165 (6% below year-end).

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists, but the signals point to a peak year. UK LLP 2022 accounts (related-party note; verified by reconciler OCR): performance fees received were £122.7m from other related parties plus £30.6m from members, £153.3m in total, against £67.4m in 2021. The draft's '£122.7m (restated)' was wrong; the figure was not restated. UK turnover was £175.2m. UK operating profit was £55.5m, an exceptional figure against £5-6m in other years. UK wages were £84.6m for 169 staff, all-in about £570k ($705k) per head. DRW Singapore profit before tax was S$70.4m vs S$24.8m. The regime was record rates and energy/commodity volatility, which is DRW's core (S&P: more rates-weighted than peers). Possible drag: the FTX/crypto crash via Cumberland. Comp-scaling: 0.7 x $705k x ~1,360 average heads gives about $671m. At 32% that implies $2.10bn. The mid is trimmed about 7% to $1.95bn because the UK's exceptional profit and pay jump point to UK (European energy-crisis) desks outperforming the group, so the UK pay proxy overstates firm pay. That trim is applied symmetrically, and 2023 is left untrimmed. Peers were mixed (Optiver +27%, IMC flat, Virtu -23%, Jump about -27%). Term-loan interest of about $25-40m is not deducted. Bars are -36%/+49%. Headcount is derived: US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 967 (+17%; welfare plan 938; amended Oct 2024 filing) and UK average staff was 169 (+80%). Bottom-up: US 967 + UK ~200 + Canada ~220 (estimated) + Singapore ~55 + other ~50, about 1,490. Average heads in 2022 about 1,360 (9% below year-end).

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. The UK cost basis was checked by the reconciler (OCR of the FY2024 accounts). The 2023 comparative shows staff costs of £76,031,909 against 244 average staff (39 technology, 79 operations and support, 126 trading), so £312k ($388k) per head is on a consistent basis. The consistency critic's 'mixed bases' concern is rejected. Comp-scaling: 0.7 x $388k x ~1,655 average heads gives about $449m. At the calibrated ~31.5% comp ratio that is about $1.42bn, raised from $1.35bn. No trim was applied, symmetric with 2022: the 45% fall in UK bonus pay per head partly reflects UK-specific normalisation and staff-mix change toward technology. DRW-specific negatives place DRW at the weak end of peers (peer net revenue -12 to -18%): UK performance fees fell to £102.7m in total (£86.5m from other related parties plus £16.2m from members; -33%), UK operating profit fell to £5.3m, and DRW Singapore profit before tax fell to S$47.7m (revenue restated to S$121m). Result: -27% year on year. A Moody's 'solid financial performance in 2023 to date' quote was relayed by a lens but its source issue was not identified; it is unverified. The FT's 'Singapore subsidiary brought in $312mn in net revenues' is S$408.8m of originally reported revenue grossed up with about S$292m of repo interest, later restated; not used. Term-loan interest of about $70-80m is not deducted. Headcount: The TRADE (3 Jul 2023) said 'roughly 1700 members of staff globally'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 1,174 (+21%); the welfare plan's 1,725 reflects a change in count basis and is not used. UK average staff was 244 (restated from 291). Bottom-up at year-end: US 1,174 + UK ~290 + Canada ~250 + Singapore/HK ~70 + other ~60, about 1,820-1,850. Revelio's 2,067 (Q4 2023) is LinkedIn-modelled and biased high. Average heads in 2023 about 1,655 (9% below year-end).

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists (FT, Nov 2024: 'Its revenue and profit figures are private'). S&P (Feb 2025): 'good, albeit lower-than-peer profitability', with 2024 results 'good, but not as strong' as competitors', because DRW is less exposed to equity volatility and more to rates. Moody's (Dec 2024): 'solid financial performance in 2024 to date'. The term loan was refinanced at $900m (Jun 2024) and upsized to $1.15bn in Dec 2024 to add trading capital (Moody's item says $200m, S&P says $250m). VC and real estate (5-10% of net revenue per S&P) are excluded. UK LLP: performance fees £135.2m (+32% vs 2023's £102.7m total; none from members), turnover £171.2m, operating profit £6.2m, all-in cost £371k ($474k) per head. DRW Singapore's profit before tax of S$91.3m was mostly a S$92.9m subsidiary dividend (S$40-44m dividends also in 2022-23). Comp-scaling: 0.7 x $474k x ~1,950 average heads gives about $647m of firm comp. At 35% (above the 32% calibration, per S&P's explicit statement that DRW lagged its peers) that implies about $1.85bn, raised from $1.80bn (at 32% it would be $2.0bn). Peers grew 24-64% (Optiver +26%, IMC +64%, Virtu +32%); DRW's +30% sits at their low end. Term-loan interest of about $80-90m is not deducted. Bars widened to -35%/+51%. Headcount: FT (Nov 2024) said 'about 2,100 staff'. US 401(k) active participants at year-end were 1,262 (about 60% of 2,100) and UK average staff was 322. Bottom-up: US 1,262 + UK ~350 + Canada ~285 + Asia ~90 + other ~70, about 2,060. Average heads in 2024 about 1,950.

Estimated; no firm-wide figure exists. Comp-scaling: 0.7 x UK all-in cost per head $528k (£150.4m / 376) x ~2,140 average heads gives about $791m. At about 36.5% comp ratio (raised from 35% because UK pay growth outran UK performance-fee growth: fee per UK head was flat at about £415k) that is about $2.17bn. Mid $2.15bn (+16%), raised from $1.95bn. The draft's trim for 'Singapore weakness' is removed. DRW Singapore's 56% fall in fair-value trading gains (S$46.2m) coincides with service-fee income rising to S$96.3m (from S$51.5m) and S$1.65bn of related-party net trading gains (nil in 2024). That points to a booking and transfer-pricing restructuring rather than weaker performance: gains plus fees were -9%. UK LLP: performance fees £155.9m (+15%), turnover £202.0m (+18%), and an operating loss of £3.5m, which is a cost-plus transfer-pricing residual and not trading PnL. DRW reports record ETF volume of $1.9T (volume, not PnL). Peers had a record year: Optiver +36%, IMC +40%, Virtu ANTI +34%, Citadel Securities +26%, HRT about +58%. DRW is kept below peer growth given S&P's description of DRW lagging peers in 2024 and the flat UK fee per head. The upper tail ($3.3bn) allows peer-median growth or more. Term-loan interest of about $90-100m is not deducted. Headcount is derived: UK average staff 376 (+54); eFC (Nov 2025, unnamed sources) gives Singapore about 100 and Hong Kong about 20; DRW Canada reported 298 full-time staff (Mar 2026 profile, probably 2025 data); US about 1,340 (estimated; plan-year 2025 Form 5500 not yet published). FIA and Wikipedia (citing Financial News) say 'over 2,000'/2,000. Revelio's Q4 2025 figure of 2,468 is LinkedIn-modelled and biased high by about 15-20%. Average heads in 2025 about 2,140.

rows.period_label: 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (Q1 2026 only; DO NOT ANNUALIZE); headcount = approximate Q1 2026 average
rows.notes:
Q1 2026 only, the latest period with any PnL data. DO NOT ANNUALIZE: the quarter mixes a large one-off North American power and gas loss with a record industry quarter, so x4 is meaningless. eFinancialCareers (4 Aug 2026; actual headline 'DRW raised pay to £340k per head in London after hiring'; wording verified by both critics) says: 'The FT reported in June that it parted ways with its North American head of power and natural gas trading... after the firm made an adjusted loss of $176m in the first quarter of 2026.' The FT article (12 Jun 2026) could not be accessed, and the draft's quoted FT headline 'Group took $176mn hit' could not be traced, so it is dropped. Moody's put the Ba2 CFR on review for downgrade on 16 Jun 2026, citing a proprietary trading-risk appetite that 'may be higher than peers' and 'above average revenue and earnings volatility'. The outcome is unknown: no TCR issue after 28 Jul 2026 is online. Scenario weights:
(a) A firm-level adjusted loss after costs, about 55%, favoured by eFC's 'the firm made' and Moody's language. Adding back about $200-290m of Q1 costs (salaries, technology, occupancy, plus desk-level bonus accrual at profitable desks) gives net trading revenue of about +$20m to +$115m.
(b) A trading-level loss, about 20%: about -$176m.
(c) A loss on the power/gas desk only, about 25%. The rest of the firm is valued at 1.0-1.3x the 2025 quarterly run-rate (about $540m), reflecting a record Q1 for market makers (Virtu Q1 ANTI $786.5m, +58.2%, verified; Citadel Securities $4.3bn; HRT $6.4bn), but tempered because DRW is less equity-volatility-exposed. Less the $176m, that gives about +$360m to +$525m.
The median is about +$75m (mid); the probability-weighted mean is about +$105m; the 90% interval is -$220m to +$480m. net_income_usd_m records the reported 'adjusted loss' of -$176m as the mid. The range runs from about -$450m (if the $176m is trading-level, so costs come on top) to about +$180m (if it is desk-level and the rest of the firm was profitable). Its definition ('adjusted') is unknown. Nothing after 31 Mar 2026 was found. Headcount, Q1 2026 average to match the PnL period: year-end 2025 about 2,200 plus modest growth gives about 2,230. drw.com (fetched Oct 2026, undated) says 'over 2,000 employees'. Revelio (Mar 2026, 2,528) and Tracxn (Sep 2026, 2,500) are LinkedIn-modelled and biased high by about 15-20%. Built In's 1,825 is undated and probably stale.

ytd_2026.description: Q1 2026 only. Do not annualize. The only 2026 PnL data point is the FT-reported (12 Jun 2026; relayed verbatim by eFinancialCareers on 4 Aug 2026) statement that DRW parted ways with its North American head of power and gas trading 'after the firm made an adjusted loss of $176m in the first quarter of 2026'. Two things are unresolved: whether the $176m is firm-wide or desk-level, and whether 'adjusted' means before or after compensation. eFC's wording and Moody's 16 Jun 2026 downgrade review (citing 'above average revenue and earnings volatility') favour a firm-level reading. The project-definition estimate of Q1 net trading revenue (before compensation) is a mid of +$75m, with a 90% interval of -$220m to +$480m, scenario-weighted. The upper tail reflects a desk-only loss in a record industry quarter (Virtu Q1 2026 ANTI +58.2%). net_income_usd_m records the reported -$176m adjusted loss (range -$450m to +$180m). No H1, Q3 or YTD figure after 31 Mar 2026 was found, and the outcome of Moody's review is unknown. Headcount is the approximate Q1 2026 average, about 2,230.

caveats: Only one firm-wide PnL figure exists: Bloomberg's FY2020 holding-level revenue of about $1.5bn and EBITDA of about $750m, sourced to people familiar during a loan process, with 'revenue' undefined. FY2019 is implied from its growth rates. Every other year is derived from partial-entity data or estimated, so bars are wide and the 2021-2025 year-to-year profile is driven by proxies, not reported results.

Gross vs net ambiguity in the FY2020 anchor. DRW's audited DRWI accounts present gross 'Total revenue' before trading expenses (12.7-22.4% of revenue), while S&P refers to 'net revenue'. The two readings are weighted roughly 50/50 and 5-10% is removed for VC and real estate. If Bloomberg's figure is gross, 2019-2020 are about 5% overstated; if it is net, about 8% understated.

The 2015-2018 rows scale one audited entity, DRW Investments, LLC, by an assumed share of group PnL: about 55% in 2015-16, 51% in 2017 and 38.5% in 2018, with ranges of 26-76%. That share is the dominant uncertainty in those rows.

2021-2025 PnL is model-derived: 0.7 (0.55-0.9) x UK LLP all-in staff cost per head x average firm headcount / comp ratio (anchored at ~32% from 2020; 35-37% in 2024-25). PnL per head for those years is therefore essentially UK pay per head x 0.7 / comp ratio, not independent evidence. PnL and headcount errors are positively correlated by construction, so a per-head band built assuming independent errors (as in build.py) overstates the per-head uncertainty slightly for these years. The UK staff mix also shifted toward technology (technology staff 39 to 75 to 111 in 2023-2025) and the UK's share of firm staff rose from about 6% (2020) to about 17% (2025), which makes the UK-to-firm pay factor less stable.

The subsidiary figures cannot be added together or read as trading PnL. They are transfer-priced: UK LLP turnover is service income plus performance fees (from affiliates and, in 2022-23, from members); the UK trading companies' results are swept by group adjustments; DRW Singapore's revenue includes intra-group service fees, subsidiary dividends and, in 2025, a booking change, and its 2022-23 figures are grossed up with repo interest. The UK LLP's 2025 operating loss is a cost-plus residual, not trading performance.

Press items traced back to their origin: the FT's 'London subsidiary made almost $1bn revenue over 2017-2018' is DRWI's $863m of total revenue before trading costs. The FT's '$312mn net revenues' for Singapore in 2023 is a gross-up artefact, later restated to S$121m.

The 2026 row covers Q1 only, to 2026-03-31. DO NOT ANNUALIZE. It rests on eFC's verbatim relay of an FT article that was not accessed. Whether the '$176m adjusted loss' is firm-wide or desk-level, and before or after compensation, is unresolved, so the row uses scenario weighting. The outcome of Moody's June 2026 downgrade review is unknown.

Term-loan interest is not deducted, for comparability with peers' net trading revenue, even though the rating agencies say the proceeds partly fund trading capital. Rough size, not reported: about $20-25m (2021), $25-40m (2022), $70-80m (2023), $80-90m (2024) and $90-100m (2025). Deducting it would lower those rows by about 2-5%.

Headcount values are approximate year-end points except 2026, which is a Q1 average. Annual averages run 2-11% below year-end in growth years; the approximate averages are in each row's notes. US 401(k) active counts are US-only floors. Canada (before the 2026 profile), Netherlands, Israel and other offices are estimated. The UK 2023 figure was restated from 291 to 244. The DOL welfare-plan count of 1,725 for 2023 reflects a change in count basis. LinkedIn-modelled aggregators (Revelio, Tracxn) run about 15-20% above bottom-up and press figures.

Cumberland DRW's only figures are SEC allegations: more than $400m of revenue and more than $27m of profit cumulatively from Mar 2018 to Oct 2024, in a case dismissed with prejudice in Mar 2025. Cumberland also moves positions to a DRW affiliate. No annual Cumberland PnL exists.

Several rating-agency quotes used qualitatively are unsourced: Moody's 'strong performance thus far in 2021' (Oct 2021 Ba2 upgrade), 'solid financial performance in 2023 to date' and 'Cumberland relatively small'. The source audit found they are not in the TCR issues the draft attributed them to. Moody's 'solid financial performance in 2024 to date' is confirmed.

Aggregator revenue figures were rejected: PrivCo ($65-250m), Owler, Growjo, RocketReach, ZoomInfo ($1bn) and AlgoTradingMap (~$5bn) are unsourced, mutually contradictory and inconsistent with the primary data.

The shared web-search budget was exhausted before both the critique and reconciliation steps, so no new searches were possible. The reconciler verified only by direct fetch or OCR: the UK LLP FY2024 accounts, the UK LLP 2022 related-party note and Virtu's Q1 2026 8-K. TCR issues after 28 Jul 2026 are not online. The Bloomberg 2021, FT 2024, FT June 2026 and Financial News 2025 originals were never fetched directly.

changelog: 2020 PnL: 1,050/1,300/1,560 -> 1,000/1,270/1,550 and pnl_basis reported_press -> derived. Partially accepted the source auditor's major challenge. The row value is a conversion of an undefined 'revenue', so 'derived' is correct. DRW's audited gross-revenue format supports a larger trading-cost haircut, but S&P's use of 'net revenue' keeps the net reading live, so the two were weighted ~50/50. The proposed $1.24bn, which effectively assumes the gross reading at ~70%, was not adopted.
2019 PnL: 690/860/1,040 -> 650/830/1,030. Partially accepted the source auditor's minor challenge, for the same gross/net reasoning (proposal 640/820/1,020).

2019 headcount: 970/1,020/1,100 -> 1,000/1,030/1,100 and basis reported_primary -> reported_press. Accepted both critics: Moody's 'over 1000 employees' (Nov 2019) is a floor, and US 401(k) counts kept rising.

2020 headcount: 990/1,080/1,190 -> 1,030/1,100/1,200. Follow-on to the 2019 floor: the bottom-up method undershot Moody's floor by about 30-50 in 2019, US 401(k) actives rose 8% in 2020, and a low below 2019's floor was implausible.

2018 PnL: 470/690/950 -> 500/760/1,100. Partially accepted the consistency critic (major). The draft's 42% DRWI share contradicted its own 34-38% cross-check, and the peer regime was strongest in 2018. Adopted a 38.5% share mid (critic: 37%; $790m) because the booking-shift argument is plausible but unproven. 2017 is unchanged.

2021-2025 comp-scaling (consistency critic, major): partially accepted. The comp-ratio anchor is reset to the ~32% that the recalibrated 2020 implies (0.7 x $542k x ~1,065 average heads = ~$405m comp on $1.27bn). Drift to 35-37% is allowed only in 2024-25, where S&P's 'not as strong as competitors' and UK pay outrunning UK fees give DRW-specific support. Judgment trims are applied symmetrically (2022 trimmed, 2023 not). A caveat now states that 2021-2025 PnL per head is model-derived and that PnL and headcount errors are positively correlated. The critic's argument that S&P's statement describes only a level captured by the 2020 calibration was rejected for 2024-25, because S&P compares DRW's 2024 results specifically with peers'.
2021 PnL: 950/1,350/1,900 -> 900/1,400/2,050. Calibrated comp ratio and the consistency critic's wider-bars challenge (accepted).

2022 PnL: 1,300/1,850/2,600 -> 1,250/1,950/2,900. Calibrated ratio ($2.10bn) less a 7% UK-energy-outperformance trim; wider bars accepted. Supported by the corrected UK evidence: £153.3m performance fees and £55.5m operating profit.

2023 PnL: 950/1,350/2,000 -> 950/1,420/2,100. Partially accepted the consistency critic (proposal 1,450/950-2,150): no extra trim, symmetric with 2022. REJECTED its 'mixed bases' claim: the reconciler OCR'd the FY2024 UK accounts, whose 2023 comparative shows staff costs of £76,031,909 against 244 average staff (39/79/126), so £312k per head is on one basis.
2024 PnL: 1,250/1,800/2,600 -> 1,200/1,850/2,800. Wider bars accepted (critic proposed 1,150/1,800/2,800); mid nudged up by the comp-ratio recalibration (35% instead of 33-38%).
